Mental Health Nursing Internship

Mental health internship — 4 weeks of supervised practice in psychiatric units: assessment, communication, safety and rehabilitation.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the objectives of a mental health internship
  • Perform mental status assessment
  • Practise therapeutic communication and safety care
  • Participate in rehabilitation and family support

In simple words

The mental health internship trains the student to communicate therapeutically, assess mental state, keep the ward safe, administer medicines and support rehabilitation.

Objectives

  • Apply the nursing process to patients with mental illness
  • Perform mental status examination and risk assessment
  • Establish a therapeutic relationship
  • Give psychiatric medicines and monitor side effects
  • Practise observation of mood, behaviour, feeding, sleep and self-care
  • Practise de-escalation and safety of the confused or violent patient
  • Support families and take part in rehabilitation activities
  • Practice ethical and legal responsibilities in psychiatric care

Skills practised

  • Mental status examination and objective documentation
  • Therapeutic communication, active listening
  • Observation of mood, behaviour, feeding, sleep and self-care
  • Medicine administration and monitoring of side effects (tremor, rigidity, weight)
  • ECT and electroconvulsive therapy supervision
  • Observation recordings, process records, incident reports
  • De-escalation, escort and seclusion as last resort
  • Rehabilitation and activity therapy
  • Team and family work

🔴 Safety first

Check for suicide and violence risk at every shift, remove the means of self-harm, and do not leave a suicidal patient alone. Confidential and accurate documentation protects the patient and the nurse.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Mental status examination guides assessment in psychiatry.
  2. Therapeutic communication is the nurse’s main tool.
  3. Always assess suicide and violence risk at each shift.
  4. Objective records and process recordings support care and legal requirements.
  5. Family education and rehabilitation are essential.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Medications include antipsychotics, antidepressants, mood stabilisers and anticholinergics.
  2. Watch for extrapyramidal signs, tardive dyskinesia and metabolic effects.
  3. Seclusion is the last resort with continuous monitoring.
  4. The nurse protects the patient’s dignity and confidentiality.
  5. Debrief with the supervisor after difficult incidents.

📌 Memory trick

Psychiatric practice: A-C-O-R — Assess, Communicate, Observe and Record.

60-second revision

  • MSE, risk assessment and documentation.
  • Therapeutic communication and relationship building.
  • Medicines and side effect monitoring.
  • Safety of suicidal and violent patients.
  • Activity therapy, family education and rehabilitation.

Test yourself

The nurse’s main tool in psychiatric care is:

Answer: B. Therapeutic communication builds trust and is the central nursing tool in psychiatry.

Suicide risk must be assessed:

Answer: B. Suicide risk is assessed at admission and regularly, every shift.

Process recording helps the student to:

Answer: B. Process recording is a written reflection of an interaction and improves communication skills.

A patient ordered haloperolol should be observed for:

Answer: A. Antipsychotics cause extrapyramidal signs such as rigidity, tremor and restlessness.

Debriefing after a difficult psychiatric incident:

Answer: B. Debriefing supports the student, prevents burnout and improves practice.
